[Fossil (He & McAuley, 2016)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) is a close structural precedent: it combines similarity-based long-term preferences with Markov-chain short-term dynamics, including higher-order history. [HGN (Ma et al., 2019)](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217) is especially relevant to gated pooling: user-conditioned feature and instance gates filter recent item embeddings before aggregation; prediction combines this representation with long-term user preferences and explicit item–item products. These establish substantial prior art for combining pooled history, recent interactions, and gating, without establishing equivalence to a particular exponential-decay SASRec extension.

[SASRec (Kang & McAuley, 2018)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) already adaptively selects relevant past interactions through attention. An exponential recency branch therefore adds a prescribed temporal bias alongside learned attention. For normalized weights w_k ∝ exp(−λk), where k=0 is newest, λ=0 gives uniform pooling and large λ approaches last-item pooling. These endpoints provide direct controls for whether intermediate recency weighting contributes useful history.

Recommended ablations, inferred from these architectural distinctions: unchanged SASRec; SASRec plus uniform pooling, last-item embedding, or exponential pooling using identical projections and fusion gates; fixed versus learned mixing; and a parameter-matched extra SASRec projection branch. Shuffle older history while preserving the last item to test order dependence, and remove the newest item from the pooled branch to test complementary historical signal. Keep history windows, loss, sampling, training budget, and evaluation candidates identical. Select using the specified four-category macro validation HR@10 and report category results; existing papers do not establish gains under this pinned benchmark.
